thread:
pagerduty-bot: 🔔 PagerDuty: HIGH - multiple 5xx errors reported from api-redwood-prod (service: inference-frontend)
Alex: getting paged too. observability shows a spike in DB connection errors and Redis acceptqueue rising. 5xxs from /v1/embeddings primarily.
Maya: confirmed. pgbouncer stats show `cl_active` ~= 1900, `max_client_conn` 2000, `cl_waiting` increasing. redis `instantaneous_ops_per_sec` up, `connected_clients` near maxclients (10k).
Jordan: are these new deploys? I don't see recent infra deploys in last 30m. could be traffic surge or leaked clients.
Alex: no deploys. traffic graph: sudden ramp from a few API keys hitting batch embeddings jobs.
incident-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-1765432199 - DB/Redis connection saturation. Assigned: oncall@sre.
Maya: quick customer impact estimate: error rate ~2.1% of requests for the last 6m, but embedding endpoints have 8-12% failure for large batched requests. A few enterprise customers are affected.
Emily: paging PD now? call flow?
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Triggered - oncall@sre. Acknowledgement pending. Escalation to second oncall in 4m if not acked.
Alex: @Maya @Jordan ok triage plan: 1) try to reduce client concurrency by applying token bucket on ingress for embeddings route; 2) temporarily disable large-batch endpoint for non-critical keys; 3) add pgbouncer burst capacity by increasing `max_client_conn` and bump app side pool; 4) if Redis accept queue is hitting kernel limits, rotate Redis read replicas or enable sentinel failover.
Jordan: running pgbouncer check now. `SHOW POOLS;` shows many idle clients stuck in `waiting` state. suspect connection leak in worker that doesn't release.
Maya: while Jordan looks, I'm going to spin up a temporary read replica and point heavy queries to it. Running playbook snippet:
```
# quick create replica (k8s job)
kubectl apply -f create-db-replica-job.yaml
# or use rds snapshot/replica flow
aws rds create-db-instance-read-replica --source-db-instance-identifier prod-db
```
Alex: Jordan, can you confirm pgbouncer config location and increase `max_client_conn` from 2000 to 3000 for immediate relief? also bump `reserve_server` slightly.
Jordan: editing config now. note: increasing max clients will increase DB backend connections; we should ensure DB has headroom. Postgres `max_connections` is 5000, so ok for short term. Applying update to pgbouncer pool config...
Emily: I've located the busiest API keys. Suggest we throttle two offending keys to 20% of their current concurrency and notify customers. drafting message to CSMs.
incident-bot: Pager duty ACK received from Alex at 1765432228.
Alex: acked and on it. Jordan, after pgbouncer bump please restart frontend worker pods gracefully to drop leaked connections. Use rolling restart with low concurrency.
Jordan: doing rolling restart now: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-frontend -n prod --grace-period=60`
Maya: spinning up read replica... creating. Also checking Redis: `INFO clients` shows `blocked_clients` rising. `maxclients` currently 10000, kernel somaxconn at default. I'm going to enable `tcp-backlog` tuning and add another Redis shard instance to share traffic.
Alex: good. also enable cache-prefetch bypass for embeddings (short-circuit heavy cache preloads) so it doesn't spike redis with cold-fill.
Emily: CSM note: "We're seeing intermittent 5xxs on embeddings; we're throttling large batch jobs and will follow up with a timeline. Please reach out to support if you see persistent failures." sending now.
Jordan: pgbouncer updated and pods restarted. `SHOW STATS;` cl_waiting dropped from ~400 to ~30. redis shard added and traffic rebalanced via proxy.
Maya: read replica came up, promoting read routing for expensive analytical queries. embedding error rate dropping to ~1% overall; large-batch down to ~3%.
Alex: good progress. remaining action: run heap check on workers to identify leak, add circuit-breaker to embeddings endpoint (fail-fast for oversized batches), and follow-up postmortem.
Emily: I'm collecting timeline and customer list for severity classification and to include in the postmortem.
incident-bot: Reminder: Escalation window passed, no further escalations.
Jordan: quick remediation commands used (for notes):
```
# increase pgbouncer clients
sed -i 's/max_client_conn = 2000/max_client_conn = 3000/' /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini && systemctl reload pgbouncer
# restart frontends
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-frontend -n prod
# check redis clients
redis-cli INFO clients | grep connected_clients
```
Alex: handoff plan: Jordan will monitor pgbouncer/pg; Maya will own Redis sharding and read replica health; Emily will own comms/CSM updates; I'll lead postmortem and coordinate root cause. If any regression, page oncall again with tag HIGH.
Emily: documenting handback in #incidents channel and creating a follow-up ticket for playbook updates (add automatic throttles for batch endpoints).
Alex: thanks team. I'll keep this thread updated; closing active mitigation once error rates <0.2% and no enterprise escalations for 30m. :white_check_mark:
